items.title: Brainfood Live On Air: GEO, What Do We Know
items.guest_line: Jen Terry Tharp · VP of Enterprise Solutions @ Jovio (panel: Alexander Chukovski, job board SEO; Kareem, co-founder @ Perception X; Devin, Pen Pixel Creative and Jovio consultant)
items.vendor_flag: Yes. Tharp and demoer Raj present Jovio's GEO advisor and AI career site 'fix' button, and Devin is a paid Jovio consultant. Kareem and Devin also sell GEO services. Chukovski says he does not.
items.reader_fit: Moderate to good: a UK in-house or agency recruiter or employer brand lead gets a concrete checklist (prompt set, consistency audit, job posting schema, candidate feedback content), but some figures are US and vendor-sourced.

points.claim: Share of voice across competitors, per AI engine and with sentiment and cited sources, is the metric to track for GEO
points.evidence: Jovio dashboard shows ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini visibility, sentiment, Glassdoor and Reddit as sources
points.quote: what is my share of voice amongst my competitors in chatbased search?

points.claim: GEO optimises for consistency across career site, social, employees and press, and the SEO playbook still matters
points.evidence: top models search the web roughly half of the time; Claude uses Brave Search, Gemini uses Google
points.quote: with GEO, we're really optimizing for consistency, right?

points.claim: Candidate feedback is the weakest owned theme with the most negative sentiment, so address ghosting and feedback policy on the career site
points.evidence: Kareem (Perception X) data grouped by attribute
points.quote: the attribute with the lowest owned share by a company but also the highest negative sentiment is candidate feedback

points.claim: Add job posting schema rather than rewriting descriptions, and pay range is expected to be the top candidate question
points.evidence: Chukovski on schema; Devin on salary range
points.quote: Just make sure that you have the job posting schema on them.

points.claim: AI Overviews now appear on about half of US transactional job queries
points.evidence: 50% stage, millions of queries tracked by Chukovski
points.quote: right now we are at a 50% stage of where an AI overview is going to appear together with Google jobs

points.claim: Most GEO consultants are selling legacy SEO
points.evidence: Chukovski, says he earns nothing from GEO consulting
points.quote: most of the geo consultants are snake oil salesmen from my perspective

points.claim: Server side rendering or static content is the one technical fix
points.evidence: Chukovski, LLMs bad at JavaScript rendering
points.quote: make sure that their website is properly server side rendered or has static content

points.claim: 77% of 300 surveyed job seekers would delegate their search to an AI agent
points.evidence: study of 300 active job seekers in seven countries, speaker not identified in captions
points.quote: 77% of them said that they they are willing to delegate their their entire job search to an AI agent

items.title: Grok Bot for Recruiters
items.guest_line: none (hosts Joe Atkinson and Jason Miller; Elise of Metaview as sponsor guest)
items.vendor_flag: Metaview is the session sponsor and Elise presents its sourcing agent and Fillmore, so those claims are vendor claims. Grok Bot (xAI) is not the hosts' product, though they run a paid community and share starter agents.
items.reader_fit: Good: a UK in-house or agency recruiter gets a concrete starter pattern (guardrails, one events agent, approval-first messaging) but the tool is early and company use needs AI policy sign-off, as the hosts say.

points.claim: Keep facts in your systems of record, not the agent's memory
points.evidence: Atkinson uses Airtable as database; same for ATS or Metaview transcripts
points.quote: facts live in your tools not the bot's memory

points.claim: Set a default approval guardrail and start with non-sensitive data
points.evidence: Atkinson: avoided PII and candidate data at first
points.quote: unless I say otherwise don't take action. So check with me first.

points.claim: Events agent for open roles grouped by job description, then Notion calendar, Slack DMs and a weekly routine
points.evidence: 14 roles put into eight groups for Metaview London
points.quote: there's 14 rolls. It's put them into eight groups.

points.claim: Do not connect the ATS; use a trusted candidate data source when demoing agents
points.evidence: Miller used the Metaview MCP only
points.quote: I did not connect it to my ATS and I used a trusted source for candidate data in Metaview

points.claim: The agent has not replaced existing tools
points.evidence: Atkinson
points.quote: actually hasn't replaced any of my tools

points.claim: Search for sales over achievement using synonyms
points.evidence: Miller: president's club, 200% attainment
points.quote: if you build out enough synonyms to overattainment like you'd be surprised what you'd find

points.claim: Metaview agent runs 50 to 100 research sub agents per candidate
points.evidence: Elise (Metaview, sponsor), vendor claim
points.quote: it is deploying kind of 50 to 100 different agents to go and run research

items.title: Continuous Improvement In TA
items.guest_line: Tony de Graaf · Co-Founder @ Recruiting Excellence Foundation
items.vendor_flag: Yes, mildly: de Graaf's foundation sells the benchmark assessment, workshops and consulting, and the episode ends by driving listeners to the survey. Pinpoint and Pebble are ad reads, not content.
items.reader_fit: Good for TA leads: a one-question prioritisation test and an AI tool ROI check are usable at any size of team, though benchmark findings are headline-level with few figures.

points.claim: Prioritise improvements by one test: impact on consistently delivering the right person on time
points.evidence: Tony de Graaf, Recruiting Excellence Foundation
points.quote: what has the biggest impact on my ability to consistently deliver the right person exactly on time

points.claim: Improvement is continuous, not a project
points.evidence: de Graaf on high performing TA teams
points.quote: An improvement mindset is continuous.

points.claim: Narrow AI tools cost setup and processing time that can cancel the saving
points.evidence: sourcing tool example, a couple hundred a month
points.quote: If you can't explain that, then it's not time to actually implement that.

points.claim: Agent plugin costs stack up quickly
points.evidence: $200 a month for a phone number and technology; 1,500 a month for one person
points.quote: asking a whooping $200 a month just for the phone number and the technology

points.claim: Almost every TA leader already knows their top issues
points.evidence: 99% claim from de Graaf's experience, anecdotal
points.quote: in my experience 99% of every TA leader I ever speak speak to they know what the big topics are

points.claim: No significant differences between regions in the benchmark
points.evidence: 21 components compared across regions
points.quote: we ran all the comparisons that we could but we could not identify. There are differences but not significant enough to call them out in the benchmark.

points.claim: Job intake was the weakest component and is not solved by technology
points.evidence: Last year's benchmark, four maturity levels
points.quote: The weakest point last year was indeed the job kickoff meeting or the job intake.
